Preview: The test is real. The motive behind it is where things get slippery.

Words I like;
Free isn't free when the guy holding the test kit also holds a commission check.
Let me save you a headache. When a company knocks on your door offering a free in-home water test, understand what's happening. Most of those tests are theater. They drop a chemical in your glass, it turns purple or foamy, and suddenly you're staring at "proof" you need to buy something today.

# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-08-11

I only received complete snapshots for 3 of the 8 competitors (Mermaid Water, EcoWater, Hampton Roads Water Services). The context was cut off before the remaining 5. I'll brief on the 3 I have and flag the gap.

# Section 1 — Executive Summary
The most aggressive competitor this week is **Mermaid Water** (Manassas, direct NoVA overlap), which is running four stacked promos—$200 off water heaters, $100 off first service, free Kinetico install, free heater flush—and has expanded into a full plumbing + pump + commercial bundle, positioning "one team for water and plumbing." **EcoWater** leans on brand authority (near-century of expertise, third-party certified, smart-home leak detection) but shows no pricing and routes everything through local dealers. **Hampton Roads Water Services** is competing on a "Lifetime Warranty" + "Made in USA" angle with a free annual water test hook, but stays vague on products and pricing. No pricing is publicly visible from any competitor except Mermaid's discount language—so promo transparency is currently a differentiation lever ClearWave can own or match.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table
| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Test first, install right, stand behind the work" (local water + plumbing) | Plumbing repair, pump/pressure systems, commercial RO/DI, Kinetico dealer | Yes — 4 promos ($200, $100, free install, free flush) | No detectable change vs. prior snapshot (identical title/meta); heavy promo stack is the standout |
| EcoWater | "Better Water Starts Here" — global leader, symptom-based diagnosis | Smart-home leak/water-conservation tech, third-party certified systems, dealer network | No | No change vs. prior snapshot (identical title/meta) |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Full Service Water Quality Experts" — peace of mind | Bacteria/virus treatment, free annual water test, Lifetime Warranty | No | No prior comparison basis; warranty + Made-in-USA framing is the lead angle |
| (5 remaining competitors) | — | — | — | Snapshots not received — data truncated |

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave
- **Counter Mermaid's promo stack:** they're winning on "clear savings now." Test a limited-time bundle (e.g., free water test + install credit) with transparent dollar amounts, since ClearWave is the only way to out-transparent the market except Mermaid.
- **Borrow the symptom-first navigation:** both EcoWater ("scale/rust/dry skin → softener") and Mermaid ("start with the result you want") route customers by problem, not product. ClearWave should add a "diagnose by symptom" homepage path if it doesn't have one.
- **Attack the warranty gap:** Hampton Roads leads with "Lifetime Warranty" but buries the details ("ask your rep"). If ClearWave can offer a clear, no-asterisk warranty and publish the terms, that's a credibility win over all three.

# Section 4 — Watch items
- **Get the 5 missing competitor snapshots** — this brief covers only 3 of 8; decisions shouldn't be made until the full set is in.
- **Mermaid:** watch whether the 4 promos persist, rotate, or add end-dates — indicates whether it's a permanent pricing strategy or a seasonal push. Also track their commercial line (RO/DI/fountains) for NoVA B2B encroachment.
- **EcoWater:** monitor the Smart Home / leak-detection push — if they add pricing or a subscription model, that's a new competitive vector.
- **Hampton Roads:** watch for any move into ClearWave's core service area and whether they ever surface pricing or productize the "annual water test" into a recurring plan.
